learning_outcomes.text: Students will be familiar with the various additive manufacturing techniques and their main technical and economic limitations.
Students will be able to choose materials and manufacturing parameters, with a view to optimizing part quality and cost.
The use of topological optimization will enable them to question an initial design and propose a more optimal one.
Distinguish between the different processes (wire, powder, liquid, polymer or metal deposition).

Distinguish between achievable renderings (surface finishes, geometric precision, mechanical strength, durability, anisotropy), and the main limitations (achievable shapes, need for supports, need for post-processing).
Implement a printing and support strategy in software such as Cura (wire deposition) or QuantAM (laser fusion on metal powder bed).
Implement the topological optimization method in software such as Inspire.

syllabus_topics: Industrial lectures (technical aspects, productivity and costs)
Free choice of study topic by students on topological optimization aspect
